question: Can the actual partial Hilbert quotient be returned to an actual smooth Meyer subrepresentation without a uniform all-zero interior strip?
status: proved at generic edges with Gevrey smoothing
current_answer: Yes. The closed retained smooth subrepresentation maps injectively and densely into Q_H; S_g factors actual convolution and has a common order-zero nuclear series. Full smooth convolution splits into actual retained and discarded smoothing operators.
method: Shrinking inner contours, whole-Xi interpolation, Cauchy–Schwarz, Gevrey domination, actual retained-jet kernel and rank-one trace cyclicity.
remaining_work: MA-PR-007 now gives adaptive actual regularized returns at every width for locally eligible tests. For an unregularized general smooth test, the exact remaining criterion is rapid decay of the attained costs in MA-PR-006; no universal bound is claimed.

question: Does this partial return remove the discarded-divisor correction or give a full return through a partial completion?
current_answer: The returned operator is B_g. The actual exterior operator E_g remains; its trace is the correction in the cutoff identity. Its removal for every test is the existing zero-location criterion.
method: Full Taylor-class operator identities and nuclear trace additivity, without comparing zero sums to construct the maps.
remaining_work: An independent proof that every relevant exterior divisor is absent would be a new zero-location argument.

context: Task1(c); boundary and unbounded common-space maps
question: Does this give the boundary-jet return or all of Meyers original off-diagonal projection maps on the narrow completion?
status: sharp return criteria proved; original-source obstruction and restricted smoothing scopes established
current_answer: PR004 gives the exact local boundary condition; PR006 gives the actual global cost criterion; PR007 gives adaptive nuclear returns. PR009–011 characterize all-test returns by finite-seminorm bounds and, after excluding proper retained factors, polynomial canonical inclusion costs. These quotient constructions do not identify every original projection entry. MO004 now identifies the rational polar correction exactly, and MO005 refutes boundedness of the original raw first diagonal on pole-free smooth theta inputs.
method: Actual finite module maps, explicit retained-jet Gram matrices, F_n=F_n P_n, adaptive damping of measured costs, entire synthesis and common rank-one trace cyclicity.
remaining_work: The all-test unregularized return retains the PR011 cost and boundary gates. MO007–008 proves genuine smaller-sum raw noninvariance. MO010–011 establishes the pole-free closure, S1 smoothing K to J and exact rank-two correction in its explicit regimes; MO012 establishes a nontrivial-character ideal endomorphism. None identifies the full original projection or removes the arithmetic deficiency. The trace of MO012 retains its actual ambient ideal projector.

context: Task1(c); arbitrary smooth tests at generic widths
question: Can actual partial factorizations approximate arbitrary compact smooth convolution without asserting an unregularized smooth return?
current_answer: Yes. Each positive-epsilon test gives an actual all-order nuclear return. Hilbert convolution converges in S1, full smooth traces converge separately, and the discarded operator traces have a limit. No convergence of return maps into Q-infinity is asserted.
method: Gaussian E approximate identity, contour decay, actual nuclear series, WP S1 bounds and M19 common rank-one trace continuity.
remaining_work: MA-PR-007 extends the regularized-return conclusion to all widths for locally eligible tests, using adaptive block damping. The exact unregularized gate is MA-PR-006; no convergence of the return maps is inferred.
